tool.title: Wireframe check at web and mobile viewports
tool.description: Render each mid-fidelity wireframe candidate of one topic at a web viewport (1280x800) and a mobile viewport (390x844). For each viewport it records `script` entries for renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each pass or fail with a note. It writes a screenshot per viewport and a report.json carrying the use, topic and surface, and exits 1 on any fail and 2 when the candidate set is not one the use admits.

inputs.name: use
inputs.description: `design` or `as-is`. Design needs at least two candidates, compared blind; as-is candidates are drawings of what renders on main, each marked `as-is` in its file name. Anything else exits 2.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.description: Which wireframe is checked: its asset directory, docs/wireframes/<topic>/ for as-is use and docs/proposals/<topic>/wireframes/ for design use (docs/wireframes/<topic>/ is also accepted there). With no candidates, every .html in it is checked; a candidate outside it is refused.

inputs.name: surface
inputs.description: What is drawn: a visualiser route key or a chrome name. Recorded in report.json; for as-is use it must be the topic itself or a ref docs/wireframes/index.json says the topic covers.

inputs.name: candidates
inputs.description: Wireframe HTML files, all in the topic's directory. Absent: every .html there. Each must carry both a web and a mobile layout (responsive CSS or two layouts).

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where screenshots and report.json go; default <the topic's directory>/checks.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: report.json: per candidate, per viewport, per criterion. The screenshots are beside it.

$comment.comment:
`use`, `topic` and `surface` are what `wireframe-design-review`'s
input contract requires (owner, 2026-10-14: the Tool takes them
rather than the contract being relaxed), and the script uses each.

The STEP, not the whole review: `wireframe-design-review`'s contract
asks for the use, topic and surface, which a renderer neither needs nor
can act on (check-tools: "the skill's own contract contradicts").

Wireframes (issue #1023): `wireframe-viewport-check`, the mechanical step of `wireframe-design-review`.
It records per-viewport pass/fail entries and never a score, because the
`wiregen` methodology adopts the structure of its source's rating and
refuses the arithmetic.
